_README: THE JUDGE FOR LOOP B. Every `expected` value here must be TRANSCRIBED BY A HUMAN (or a model with a cited source) from published NASA/Espenak local-circumstances output or Jubier's interactive maps. A value the solver produced is NOT ground truth — it is the thing under test. gate_b.py REFUSES TO RUN while any anchor is unpopulated. This is structural: it makes fabricating ground truth impossible rather than merely forbidden.
_how_to_populate: 1. Open NASA/Espenak local circumstances (or Jubier's map) for the eclipse date.
2. Enter the observer lat/lon exactly as given below.
3. Transcribe: time of max eclipse (UT), sun altitude at max, duration of totality, in_umbra.
4. Record the URL you read it from in `source`.
Do NOT round. Do NOT infer. If a source doesn't give a value, leave it null and note why.

_provenance.populated_by: Claude (Opus 4.8) on 2026-07-18, per human instruction 'I gather + cite all of them'. Values transcribed from external published sources listed per anchor; NONE derived from the solver under test (src/besselian.py) or the cross-checker (src/crosscheck_skyfield.py).
_provenance.sourcing_rule_followed: Where a published source reported a field only at whole-degree precision (e.g. IGN sun altitude '4 deg'), the graded field `sun_alt_deg` was left null rather than frozen, because a whole-degree value cannot be validated against the 0.10 deg modern tolerance without manufacturing a false failure. The coarse value is preserved in `_source_values` for the record. This follows _how_to_populate rule 5.
_provenance.known_gap: Precise (0.1 deg) sun altitude at exact anchor coordinates is only populated for Burlington 2024 (nationaleclipse.com per-city page, coordinates matching the anchor to 5 decimals). The definitive per-coordinate source for the others (Xavier Jubier's calculator; timeanddate per-city altitude) blocks automated fetches. Follow-up task: transcribe Jubier altitudes for the Spain and high-sun anchors to widen altitude coverage — especially Castellon, the in-person canary.

ancient._note: Position tolerance is NOT a fixed number. It is the delta-T uncertainty band from outputs/delta_t_decision.json for that era. Earth turns 15 deg/hour: a 1-hour delta-T error moves the path ~1500 km. Report the band; do not pretend to precision you do not have.

crosscheck_besselian_vs_skyfield._note: Two independent methods must agree with EACH OTHER, tighter than either agrees with published values.

deferred_anchors.why: DELTA-T STRESS TEST. The point is not to nail the position — it is to confirm the engine's error stays inside the documented uncertainty band from B2. Suspiciously tight agreement is itself a red flag: it means delta-T is being applied twice, or not at all.
